entry.title: Guidance Required on BAdI for Updating Supplier Invoice Item-Level Custom Fields via A2A API
entry.content:
Hi Experts,

In SAP S/4 HANA Public Cloud, we have a requirement to read the reference Purchase Order (PO) details while creating a supplier invoice from a third-party system and use those details to update item-level custom fields in the Manage Supplier Invoices application.

Initially, we identified the BAdI LOG_EDI_MM_INVOICE_CE_MAP. However, this BAdI is intended for B2B integration, whereas our third-party system uses the A2A service. Therefore, the BAdI is not triggered when creating a supplier invoice through the API.

We also explored an alternative approach by manually posting or parking supplier invoices in SAP and attempting to update the custom field values using the following BAdIs:

  • MRM_MRIS_DATA_MODIFY_CE

  • MRM_MRDC_DATA_MODIFY_CE

  • MRM_ERS_DATA_MODIFY_CE

However, none of these BAdIs is triggered during the supplier invoice posting or parking process.

Could you please suggest the appropriate BAdI or enhancement option to retrieve the reference PO details from the supplier invoice and update the item-level custom fields in Manage Supplier Invoices, particularly when invoices are created through the A2A API?

Any relevant SAP documentation, knowledge base articles, or technical blogs addressing this scenario would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks in advance for your support.

Best regards,

entry.title: Purchase Order Accruals calculation
entry.content:
Dear All,

We onboard a consultant on a six-month contract with a daily rate of GBP 100. As per the contract agreement, the maximum billable days are limited to 22 days per month.

We do not use the Service Entry Sheet (SES) concept in SAP. Therefore, we need to manage the Purchase Order (PO) and monthly accrual postings without service entry confirmations.

We are facing the following challenges:

Scenario 1: Maintaining the PO quantity as 6 months

If we maintain the PO order quantity as six months, the system calculates the PO value based on 180 days × GBP 100, resulting in GBP 18,000. This is incorrect because the contractual maximum is 22 billable days per month.

The system also calculates accruals based on the actual calendar days in each month (30 or 31 days), resulting in incorrect accrual amounts.

Scenario 2: Maintaining the PO quantity as 132 days

If we maintain the PO order quantity as 132 days (22 days × 6 months), the PO value is correctly calculated as GBP 13,200.

However, the accrual calculation is still incorrect. For example, for October 2026, SAP calculates an accrual of GBP 3,100 (31 calendar days × GBP 100) instead of the expected GBP 2,200 (22 billable days × GBP 100).

Clarification Required

How can we achieve the correct PO valuation and monthly accrual calculations using standard SAP functionality, considering that we do not use Service Entry Sheets?

Our requirements are:

Maintain the PO value at GBP 13,200 for the six-month contract.
Calculate monthly accruals based on 22 billable days, resulting in GBP 2,200 per month.
Prevent the system from calculating accruals based on calendar days.
Use standard SAP PO and accrual functionality without custom development, wherever possible.
Please advise on the recommended standard SAP configuration and process to ensure that both the PO value and monthly accrual postings are aligned with the contractual terms, without using the Service Entry Sheet process.

 

Thanks

Naveen

entry.title: ultiple Batches in One Inspection Lot (QM Type 10) - S/4HANA Cloud
entry.content:
Hi SAP Community,

We are currently implementing SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and facing a requirement regarding Quality Management (QM) integration with Sales and Distribution (SD) for inspection type 10 (Inspection for Outbound Delivery).

When an outbound delivery is created for a sales order line item, and the batch determination assigns multiple physical batches (CHARG) of the same material (e.g., 3 different batches allocated to cover the line item quantity), the system automatically creates one inspection lot per physical batch.

Our business requirement is to group these multiple physical batches into a single inspection lot per delivery/item, rather than having the system generate separate inspection lots for each batch assigned to the delivery.

Configuration Checked:

We evaluated the settings in Define Default Values for Inspection Types under the Inspection Lot Summary (Resumen lote insp.) field:

  • One inspection per material/batch and ref. doc.
  • One inspection per material/batch and inbound delivery
  • One inspection per material/batch

As per our understanding, all these standard options strictly maintain the primary key combination of Material + Batch (CHARG), making it impossible to consolidate different batches under one inspection lot natively through this setting.

Questions:

  1. Is there any standard functionality or alternative workflow in S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition to achieve a single inspection lot across multiple batches for delivery inspections?
  2. If this is a hard constraint due to inventory traceability (DE/Usage Decision per CHARG), what is the recommended SAP Best Practice to streamline the result recording and Usage Decision process for multi-batch delivery items without duplicating QM operational tasks?

Thanks in advance for your support and insights!

#qualitymanagement

@Lakshmipathi @CarrieMason

entry.title: How to Access Data from Unreleased CDS Views for Reporting Purposes?
entry.content:
Hi Experts,

We have a reporting requirement and would appreciate guidance on the standard SAP approach.

We need to use the CDS view I_NotificationCause in a report because it contains the field NotificationCauseText, which is required by the business. We can see the CDS view and its data in Eclipse, but it is not released for Key User Extensibility or Developer Extensibility.

Because the CDS view is not released, we are unable to consume it in a supported way for reporting purposes.

My questions are:

  • What is the standard SAP-recommended solution in this scenario?
  • If the CDS view is available and the data is visible in Eclipse, why is it not released for customer consumption?
  • What is the purpose of providing such CDS views if they cannot be used in reporting or extensibility scenarios?
  • Is there any supported mechanism to access NotificationCauseText when I_NotificationCause is not released?
  • Can customers request SAP to release a CDS view, or is there any official process for that?
  • Are there any alternative released CDS views or standard SAP objects that provide the same information and can be used for reporting?

As a functional consultant, it is difficult to explain to business users why the required data exists in the system and is visible in eclipse, but cannot be consumed in a supported report due to release restrictions.

Our primary objective is to build a report, so if I_NotificationCause is intentionally not released, could you please suggest any alternative released CDS view that contains the NotificationCauseText or equivalent functionality?

Any guidance on SAP's recommended best practice would be highly appreciated.

Thank you.

entry.title: Missing Profit Center in G/L Line Items for Year-End Closing/Opening Documents (Italian Localization
entry.content:
Hello SAP Experts,

We are facing an issue with the year-end closing/opening documents (Document Type CL) in the Italian localization on SAP S/4HANA.

When using the "Display Line Items in General Ledger" app (F2217) for balance sheet accounts, the Profit Center field is completely blank for these closing/opening postings.
However, if we check the "Trial Balance" app, the balances are correctly carried forward and the Profit Center is accurately populated (e.g., an account with a 168k balance correctly shows Profit Center 'GENER' at 31/12 and 01/01 in the Trial Balance).

We have already checked the physical accounting document (Doc. Type CL) and confirmed that the Profit Center is indeed missing from the generated line items, which explains why the F2217 app cannot display it. Since our regulatory reporting heavily relies on the Line Items app, this missing analytical dimension is a blocking issue for our business users.

My questions are:

Why does the standard Italian closing/opening program aggregate these balances without carrying over the Profit Center dimension to the physical document line items?

How can we fix or configure the system for the future so that year-end closing/opening documents inherit and display the correct Profit Center at the line item level?

Thank you in advance for your support.

entry.title: HR Data Confidentiality / Masking & Document Splitting impact on F24 Tax Payments (Italian Localizat
entry.content:
Hello SAP Experts,
We are submitting a high-priority request on behalf of our Management regarding the treatment of HR/Payroll postings and their impact on the Balance Sheet in our SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud environment.

Currently, our payroll costs are posted across several detailed G/L accounts distinguishing between regular employees and executives (e.g., 61010000 Paghe dirigenti, 61010001 Paghe agenti, 61060000 TFR Dirigenti, etc.). Furthermore, these postings are strictly allocated to specific Cost Centers and Profit Centers to comply with mandatory regulatory accounting (Separazione Contabile).

Requirement 1: HR Data Confidentiality & Reporting
Management requires that general finance users only see an aggregated, single monthly line item for personnel costs (hiding the distinction between executives/regular staff and masking the specific Profit/Cost Centers). However, a restricted group of users (Controlling/Regulatory team) must retain the ability to view the fully detailed line items (with specific G/L, Cost Center, and Profit Center) for regulatory reporting purposes.Question 1: What is the best practice or standard functionality in S/4HANA Public Cloud (e.g., Authorization Objects, Data Masking, specific Fiori reporting roles) to achieve this dual-level visibility for HR postings without losing the analytical detail in the Universal Journal?

Requirement 2: Balance Sheet Clearing and F24 Payment
We also need to evaluate the impact of this setup on the balance sheet. Currently, the HR payables/receivables are correctly loaded onto specific detailed Profit Centers. However, the F24 tax payment model is posted entirely to a generic Profit Center ("GENER"). Because of this, the liabilities are cleared at the vendor/tax authority level, but the balances on the specific Profit Centers remain open.Question 2: How can we ensure that the F24 payment clears the balances on the specific Profit Centers automatically? Is an Expert Configuration required to enforce the "Zero Balance" indicator for the Profit Center characteristic in the Document Splitting configuration?
Thank you for your prompt support and guidance.
